requirements.quote:
An endpoint sends a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame (type=0x19) to
   indicate that it will no longer use a connection ID that was issued
   by its peer.  This includes the connection ID provided during the
   handshake.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for a connection ID issued by its peer, including one provided during the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The frame indicates that the endpoint will no longer use the identified connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send the frame and verify that the sender ceases using the retired peer-issued connection ID.

requirements.quote:
Retiring a connection ID invalidates the stateless reset token
   associated with that connection ID.
requirements.condition: When a connection ID is retired.
requirements.required_behavior: Invalidate the stateless reset token associated with that connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue treating the associated stateless reset token as valid.
requirements.why_checkable: Token validity can be inspected or exercised after retirement of the associated connection ID.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the frame as an integer Type field fixed to 0x19 followed by an integer Sequence Number field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame with a type other than 0x19 or with a different field order.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized frames can be inspected to verify the fixed type value, required sequence-number field, and field ordering.

requirements.quote:
Sequence Number:  The sequence number of the connection ID being
      retired; see Section 5.1.2.
requirements.condition: When processing the Sequence Number field of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the field as the sequence number of the connection ID being retired.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed sequence number can be compared with the connection ID selected for retirement.

requirements.quote:
Receipt of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame containing a sequence number
   greater than any previously sent to the peer MUST be treated as a
   connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: Upon receipt of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame whose sequence number is greater than every sequence number previously sent to that peer.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can be sent a frame with an unsent sequence number above the prior maximum and the resulting connection error can be asserted.

requirements.quote:
The sequence number specified in a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST
   NOT refer to the Destination Connection ID field of the packet in
   which the frame is contained.  The peer MAY treat this as a
   connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When sending a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame in a packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The frame's sequence number must not identify the connection ID used in the packet's Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.why_checkable: An emitted packet's Destination Connection ID can be mapped to its sequence number and compared with the frame's sequence number.

requirements.quote:
The sequence number specified in a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST
   NOT refer to the Destination Connection ID field of the packet in
   which the frame is contained.  The peer MAY treat this as a
   connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: Upon receipt of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame whose sequence number refers to the Destination Connection ID field of its containing packet.
requirements.error_behavior: The peer is permitted to treat the violation as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted packet can trigger the condition and verify that PROTOCOL_VIOLATION is an accepted response, though the response is optional.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint cannot send this frame if it was provided with a zero-
   length connection ID by its peer.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint was provided a zero-length connection ID by its peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: After configuring a peer with a zero-length connection ID, emitted frames can be inspected for absence of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID.

requirements.quote:
length connection ID by its peer.  An endpoint that provides a zero-
   length connection ID MUST treat receipt of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID
   frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: Upon receipt of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame by an endpoint that provided a zero-length connection ID.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame can be delivered after the receiver supplies a zero-length connection ID, and the resulting error type can be asserted.
